title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Efficiency, accessibility, climate change and disaster resiliency, and sustainability of safe water and sanitation improved in the GHA, and the towns of Auki, Gizo, Munda, Noro, and Tulagi

14,000 households (64%) in GHA access improved on-site sanitation policies and fecal sludge management. (2019 baseline: 0 households) (OP 3.3.2) Progress/Status: Progress towards achieving the target of 14,000 households in greater Honiara benefiting from improved onsite sanitation policies is on track following the preparation of the draft greater Honiara Area Comprehensive Sanitation Plan 2022 - 2026. The draft Plan now requires ratification by Honiara City Council and Guadalcanal Province before the finalization of septage treatment plant design (design scheduled to be completed by Q3 2025). Data Source: Honiara City Council Environmental Health Unit reports Actual value:

SIWA continues to recover its annual O&M costs, asset depreciation costs, and debt servicing costs from user charges and government community service obligation payments (2019 baseline: 100%) (OP 4.1.1) Progress/Status: Full recovery of annual operation and maintenance costs, asset depreciation costs, and debt servicing costs from user charges and government community service obligation payments is essential for SW's financial sustainability. SW achieved full cost recovery in 2020 and 2023 and just fell short of the target (by less than 3%) in 2022. The 2024 financial reports have yet to be audited but the unaudited statements indicate full cost recovery in 2024. SIWA is implementing further measures to strengthen the financial sustainability of SW including annual cost of service and tariff reviews, and equally important, further investments to reduce nonrevenue water. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and SIWA annual audit reports Actual value:

2,000 households in GHA are connected to a sewer network. (2019 baseline: 600 households) (OP 4.1) Progress/Status: At end February 2024, 648 households were connected to the SW's sewerage networks down from 661 households in August 2023. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and Pacific Water Utility Benching Report, Pacific Water and Wastewater Association, published annually Actual value:

Nonrevenue water in GHA is reduced to 30% (2019 baseline: 62%) (OP 4.2.2) Progress/Status: NRW across all SIWA water supply networks averaged 59.4% from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024, marginally down from the national NRW 2023 average of 59.9%. The average NRW for the greater Honiara area for 2024 was 59.5% (marginally lower than the 2023 average of 60.1%). Overall, the project is off-track to reach the project NRW target in Honiara of 30% or less by 2027. Lack of progress on NRW is driven by primarily by aging infrastructure. Substantial investments are required to reduce NRW including expediting water main renewals. The project currently targets the replacement of 10km of trunk water mains in Honiara with high leakage. Investigations in 2022 indicate that about 50km of water mains in Honiara suffer substantial leakage and require replacement. Further investments are also required to reduce commercial losses (primarily illegal connections and water meters inaccuracies). Data Source: SIWA annual report; and Pacific Water Utility Benching Report, Pacific Water and Wastewater Association, published annually Actual value:

By July 2028: 16,500 households, including 12% households headed by women, use improved and climate- and disaster-resilient water supplies. (2019 baseline: 9,000) (OP 2.4.1, OP 3.2.5, OP 4.1) Progress/Status: SW has surpassed the project's water supply coverage target of 16,500 households with 16,705 households connected at the end of February 2024 representing an 86% increase in the number of connected households since project appraisal in May 2019. Over the 12 months since February 2023, SW has connected an additional 668 households to its water supply networks or which 94% (626 connections) were in the greater Honiara area. There have also been improvements in drinking water quality compliance with water safety plans across SW operations. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and SIWA water production records released monthly Actual value:

Sewage discharged from the sewer system complies with water quality standards in GHA. (2019 baseline: 0%) (OP 3.3.4) Progress/Status: The water quality compliance target for sewage discharged from the Honiara sewer systems is likely to be achieved if the works to reconfigure the sewer system proceed. The design of the sewerage rehabilitation and outfall construction contract for the eastern-area system is current being reviewed by SW's engineering design consultant and procurement may proceed in Q2 2025. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and Pacific Water Utility Benching Report, Pacific Water and Wastewater Association, published annually Base year: 2019 Baseline value: N/A
